c_immune_response: Protection mediated by both humoral (immune serum) and cellular (splenic lymphocytes) immunity; combined effects not additive beyond early time points; serum reduced initial spleen colonization when injected before challenge. [Ref6993:Plommet et al, 1986]
c_vaccination_protocol: Mice were vaccinated intravenously with the Brucella abortus cell-wall peptidoglycan fraction (PG). [Ref6993:Plommet et al, 1986]

[Ref6993:Plommet et al, 1986]

c_description: Transfer of immune serum and splenic cells from vaccinated mice to naive DBA/2 mice followed by intravenous challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 544; spleen and liver bacterial counts performed weekly up to six weeks. [Ref6993:Plommet et al, 1986]

c_vaccination_protocol: Beef heifers were vaccinated on Day 0 with chemically modified salt-extractable protein (dCSP) from Brucella abortus Strain 19 in Freund's complete adjuvant; a booster was given six weeks later with either homologous or heterologous vaccine. [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_protection_efficacy: No significant protection observed; 60 to 83% of vaccinated heifers aborted and 70-83% were culture positive after challenge, similar to controls [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_challenge_protocol: Vaccination of beef heifers followed by serologic tests, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, fluorometric immunoassay, lymphocyte blast transformation assay, and intraconjunctival challenge with Brucella abortus strain 2308. [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_description: Vaccination of beef heifers followed by serologic tests, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, fluorometric immunoassay, lymphocyte blast transformation assay, and intraconjunctival challenge with Brucella abortus strain 2308 [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]

c_protection_efficacy: Transferred lymph node and spleen cells conferred immunity reducing Brucella counts; lymph node cells were more efficient; immunity increased for about 21 days post-transfer; immunity was partially abrogated by anti-Thy serum treatment; genetic background influenced response. c_challenge_protocol: Adoptive transfer of splenic or popliteal lymph node cells from vaccinated DBA/2 donor mice to recipient mice challenged intravenously with virulent Brucella abortus; spleen and liver bacterial counts measured at 15 days or later. [Ref6997:Plommet et al, 1987]
c_description: Adoptive transfer of splenic or popliteal lymph node cells from vaccinated DBA/2 donor mice to recipient mice challenged intravenously with virulent Brucella abortus; spleen and liver bacterial counts measured at 15 days or later. [Ref6997:Plommet et al, 1987]

c_description: Immune serum from vaccinated mice was injected into mice before or after challenge with virulent Brucella abortus 544; effects on bacterial dissemination and clearance in spleen and liver were measured over time. [Ref7004:Plommet et al, 1983]

c_challenge_protocol: Mouse protection test using monoclonal antibodies against B. ovis OMPs and R-LPS, with challenge by B. ovis strain 63/290. [Ref7014:Bowden et al, 1995]
c_description: Mouse protection test using monoclonal antibodies against B. ovis OMPs and R-LPS, with challenge by B. ovis strain 63/290. [Ref7014:Bowden et al, 1995]

c_description: Mouse vaccination followed by challenge with virulent Brucella abortus; in vitro splenocyte proliferation assay with thioredoxin-Cu/Zn SOD fusion protein stimulation. [Ref7037:Oñate et al, 1999]

c_immune_response: SBP immunization induced CD4+ T cells producing IL-2 and IL-4 but no detectable IFN-gamma, indicating a Th2-type response; live Brucella infection induced CD4+ T cells producing IFN-gamma and IL-2 but not IL-4, indicating a Th1-type response associated with protective immunity. [Ref7016:Zhan et al, 1995]
c_description: T cell cytokine production was analyzed in spleen cells from mice immunized with SBP versus Brucella-infected mice; limiting dilution analysis of CD4+ T cells; adoptive transfer of IFN-gamma or IL-4 producing CD4+ T cells to recipient mice followed by challenge infection. [Ref7016:Zhan et al, 1995]

c_immune_response: High IgG antibody titers with predominant IgG1 subclass indicating mixed Th1/Th2 response; strong Th1 cytokine (IFN-γ) production; increased lymphocyte proliferation indicating enhanced cellular immunity. [Ref7203:Singh et al, 2015a]
c_vaccination_protocol: Immunization of mice followed by measurement of IgG antibody titers, IgG subclass analysis, Th1 cytokine (IFN-γ) production, lymphocyte proliferation assay, and enumeration of splenic CFU after. [Ref7203:Singh et al, 2015a]

c_challenge_protocol: Immunization of mice followed by measurement of IgG antibody titers, IgG subclass analysis, Th1 cytokine (IFN-γ) production, lymphocyte proliferation assay, and enumeration of splenic CFU after challenge with Brucella abortus 544. [Ref7203:Singh et al, 2015a]
c_description: Immunization of mice followed by measurement of IgG antibody titers, IgG subclass analysis, Th1 cytokine (IFN-γ) production, lymphocyte proliferation assay, and enumeration of splenic CFU after challenge with Brucella abortus 544. [Ref7203:Singh et al, 2015a]

c_description: BALB/c mice were vaccinated with modified and nonmodified BCSP proteins, then challenged with virulent Brucella abortus 2308; sera were tested for IgM and IgG antibodies by ELISA; spleen CFU and splenomegaly were measured. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]

c_immune_response: IgG serologic responses to homologous and heterologous proteins were altered by chemical modification. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]
c_protection_efficacy: Chemical modification had no effect on protection induced by recombinant proteins. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]
c_challenge_protocol: BALB/c mice vaccinated with modified recombinant proteins were challenged with virulent Brucella abortus 2308; sera tested for IgM and IgG antibodies by ELISA. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]
c_description: BALB/c mice vaccinated with modified recombinant proteins were challenged with virulent Brucella abortus 2308; sera tested for IgM and IgG antibodies by ELISA. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]

c_immune_response: Protection mediated by both T lymphocytes and antibodies, with antibodies playing a substantially greater role; antibodies specific for HS proteins were predominantly IgG2a and IgG3 isotypes; immune responses targeted protein moieties of HS; rough lipopolysaccharide component was poorly immunogenic in BALB/c mice. [Ref7022:Jiménez et al, 1994]
c_protection_efficacy: HS-QS-21 vaccine afforded protection against B. ovis challenge as good as that developed after primary infection and as good as or better than that provided by attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref7022:Jiménez et al, 1994]
c_challenge_protocol: Protection was evaluated in BALB/c mice by challenge infection; passive transfer assays assessed roles of antibodies and T lymphocytes; comparison made with immunity from primary infection and with attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref7022:Jiménez et al, 1994]
c_description: Protection was evaluated in BALB/c mice by challenge infection; passive transfer assays assessed roles of antibodies and T lymphocytes; comparison made with immunity from primary infection and with attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref7022:Jiménez et al, 1994]

c_immune_response: LPS from Brucella abortus acts as a T-cell-independent type 1 (TI-1) carrier antigen, eliciting humoral immune responses including IgG subclass antibodies even in T-cell deficient mice, indicating its ability to directly stimulate B cells. [Ref7024:Betts et al, 1993]
c_protection_efficacy: TNP-LPS-BA generated anti-TNP antibody responses in various mouse strains including immunodeficient mice, with higher titers of IgG1, IgG2a, and IgG2b antibodies in C3H/HeJ mice compared to TNP-LPS from E. coli; LPS-BA stimulated B cells more effectively than LPS-EC in C3H/HeJ mice. [Ref7024:Betts et al, 1993]
c_description: Immunization of normal and immunodeficient mice with TNP-LPS-BA and comparison of antibody responses to known T-dependent and T-independent antigens; measurement of immunoglobulin G subclasses and B cell proliferative responses. [Ref7024:Betts et al, 1993]

c_protection_efficacy: The 18 kD OMP protected 66.7% of experimental animals against brucellosis, compared to 78.0% protection by the commercial live vaccine. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]
c_description: In vivo experiments in mice assessing protection and infectious process progression. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]

c_protection_efficacy: The 38 kD OMP did not provide protective activity; the infectivity index and colony forming units in spleen were higher in vaccinated animals than controls. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]
c_description: In vivo experiments in mice assessing protection and infectious process progression. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]

c_immune_response: Vaccination stimulated marked antibody responses and increased cell-mediated immune response measured by lymphocyte blast transformation; antibody responses increased rapidly after challenge and were higher in heifers that aborted; LBT responses were higher in vaccinates but not significantly different from controls [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_vaccination_protocol: Beef heifers were vaccinated on Day 0 with salt-extractable protein (CSP) from Brucella abortus Strain 19 in Freund's complete adjuvant; a booster was given six weeks later with either homologous or heterologous vaccine. [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_protection_efficacy: No significant protection observed; 60 to 83% of vaccinated heifers aborted and 70-83% were culture positive after challenge, similar to controls [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_challenge_protocol: Vaccination of beef heifers followed by serologic tests, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, fluorometric immunoassay, lymphocyte blast transformation assay, and intraconjunctival challenge with Brucella abortus strain 2308. [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_description: Vaccination of beef heifers followed by serologic tests, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, fluorometric immunoassay, lymphocyte blast transformation assay, and intraconjunctival challenge with Brucella abortus strain 2308 [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]

[Ref7026:Pugh et al, 1996]

[Ref7026:Pugh et al, 1996]
c_challenge_protocol: BALB/c mice were vaccinated with the protein fractions and later challenged with Brucella abortus 2308; protection was assessed by measuring colony-forming units (CFU) in spleens and spleen size; serologic responses were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). [Ref7026:Pugh et al, 1996]
c_description: BALB/c mice were vaccinated with the protein fractions and later challenged with Brucella abortus 2308; protection was assessed by measuring colony-forming units (CFU) in spleens and spleen size; serologic responses were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). [Ref7026:Pugh et al, 1996]

c_immune_response: Serum antibody titers peaked at PID 14; marked germinal center formation and medullary plasmacytosis by PID 28; brucellar antigens detected in capsular granulomas; bacteria found mainly in macrophages and small lymphocytes. [Ref7027:Cheville et al, 1996]

c_description: In vitro susceptibility assays to H2O2 and paraquat; in vivo spleen colonization and immune response studies in BALB/c mice. [Ref7029:Robertson et al, 1996]

c_immune_response: Activation of classical and mannose-binding lectin complement pathways leading to complement deposition (iC3b, C5b-9) and bacterial killing; alternative pathway not activated. [Ref7046:Fernandez-Prada et al, 2001]

[Ref7046:Fernandez-Prada et al, 2001]

c_immune_response: Both humoral and cellular immunity were stimulated by the vaccine. High titers of Brucella 104M-specific IgG2a antibodies were detected, higher than IgG1. Cytokines IFN-γ, IL-18, and IL-1β concentrations in serum and lung homogenate were significantly elevated in immunized groups before challenge. After challenge, serum cytokine levels decreased compared to controls, while lung cytokine levels remained elevated. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]
c_vaccination_protocol: Female BALB/c mice aged 6–8 weeks were immunized with Brucella abortus 104M using three experimental routes: intratracheal aerosol, intranasal instillation, and subcutaneous injection. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]
c_protection_efficacy: Immunized mice showed no abnormal clinical symptoms or significant body weight changes. Spleen weights post-challenge were significantly lower in immunized groups compared to controls. Bacterial loads in spleens decreased over time and were significantly lower than controls after challenge. High titers of specific antibodies were detected, peaking at week 8. Cytokine levels (IFN-γ, IL-18) were elevated pre-challenge and modulated post-challenge. No significant differences were observed among immunization routes. The vaccine showed obvious protective efficacy against aerosol challenge. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]
c_challenge_protocol: At 22 weeks post-immunization, mice were challenged with Brucella A19 via intratracheal aerosol. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]
c_description: Female BALB/c mice aged 6-8 weeks were immunized by the three routes. Clinical manifestations, body weight, spleen weight, bacterial loads in spleens, serum anti-Brucella antibody titers, and cytokine concentrations (IFN-γ, IL-18) in serum and lung homogenate were measured at 4, 8, 16, and 24 weeks post-immunization. At 22 weeks post-immunization, mice were challenged with Brucella A19 via intratracheal aerosol. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]
